paras: The attempted lynching of Albert Smartt took place on the night of August 16, 1888, when a mob of Black men at Tullahoma, Tennessee, organized to lynch Smartt, a Black prisoner accused of killing his brother-in-law, Samuel Strabler. An officer outwitted the mob and drove Smartt to the jail at Manchester, and the dispatch reporting the episode ran under the headline "A Mob Thwarted."

Smartt was charged with killing Strabler, his brother-in-law; the dispatch gives no date or circumstances for that killing and does not give Strabler's race. He was in custody, and his preliminary examination was going on at Tullahoma when the mob formed.

According to a Nashville dispatch dated August 17, a mob "composed of co'ored men" was organized at Tullahoma the night before to lynch Smartt and went to the building where the examination was being held. Justice Thomas, who held the examination, remanded Smartt to jail without bond. An officer who learned the mob was there led "the angry negroes" to believe that Smartt would be kept in town under a guard of only two men. Instead, the officer slipped the prisoner out, drove him by buggy to Manchester, and had him lodged in jail there.

The dispatch said the mob was "indignant" at the removal and that another attempt to lynch Smartt at Manchester was possible because "the feeling against him is very strong." No report of a second attempt, of arrests of mob members, or of Smartt's trial appears in the coverage.

The episode survives in a single wire item, printed on August 25 on page 2 of The Forrest City Times, an Arkansas weekly. The dispatch called Smartt "the negro who killed Samuel Strabler," stating his guilt as fact before any trial, and it credited the officer's ruse under the headline "A Mob Thwarted." It named the race of both the mob and its target but did not present the attempt as racial, and it did not comment on the mob beyond calling its members "angry" and "indignant." No Tennessee report of the episode, and no Black-press coverage, was found.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of Albert Smartt
bases: A mob organized to lynch a prisoner accused of killing, went to his preliminary examination, and was foiled when an officer removed him to another jail (A1).

A mob organized to lynch Smartt over the killing of his brother-in-law, but an officer removed him to the Manchester jail and no one was killed (A1); this was a thwarted attempt, not a completed lynching.
The episode is known from one wire dispatch from Nashville, printed in an Arkansas weekly (A1).
